sprint.goal: Add JWT-based user authentication: login, register, protect task endpoints

sprint_history.goal: Build a lightweight Kanban project management app: REST API + minimal web UI. Users can create tasks, move them between Todo, In Progress, and Done, edit task details, and delete tasks.

tasks.title: Create tasks table schema (id, title, status, created_at) in database.py
Implement REST API in server.py: create/list/update/delete tasks, move between statuses
Build Kanban board UI in index.html (3 columns, click-to-move) consuming the API

messages.content: database.py now exposes initialize_database(), get_connection(), utc_timestamp(), DATABASE_PATH, and VALID_STATUSES; tasks uses id, title, status, created_at with valid statuses todo/in_progress/done.

API ready: GET/POST /api/tasks; PATCH or PUT /api/tasks/:id; DELETE /api/tasks/:id. Tasks return id, title, status (todo|in_progress|done), created_at. POST requires title and accepts optional status; PATCH accepts title and/or status.
Frontend is complete and consumes the implemented task API; the board supports Todo, In Progress, and Done workflows.

QA found a minor UX gap: edit-form submission closes the dialog even when the PATCH request fails because mutate() catches errors internally. Keeping it open on failed saves would let users retry immediately.

Security review passed: API limits JSON request bodies, validates task fields/statuses, uses SQLite parameters for values, escapes frontend task text via textContent, and constrains static files to the static directory.

sprint_history.retrospective: Sprint retrospective: Architecture established the stdlib contract; database delivered the constrained schema; backend implemented validated CRUD; frontend integrated the three-column board; QA added and passed lifecycle coverage while noting the failed-save dialog UX gap; security verified input, SQL, rendering, and static-path safeguards; manager coordinated the completed handoffs.

tasks.title: Define the standard-library authentication design: user model, password hashing, signed JWT claims/expiry, API contract, and task ownership rules.
Add a users schema and migrate task ownership in database.py, including unique usernames and secure password-hash storage fields.
Implement register/login endpoints, standard-library JWT signing and verification, and Bearer-token protection plus per-user scoping for task endpoints in server.py.
Add register/login UI and authenticated task requests in static/index.html, retaining a token only for the browser session and handling unauthenticated responses.
Add regression coverage for registration, login, token expiry/invalid-token rejection, protected task endpoints, and task isolation between users.
Review password hashing, JWT signing/verification, token handling, authorization boundaries, and auth error responses after implementation.

architecture_decisions.decision: Python stdlib http.server + sqlite3 for backend, single static HTML+vanilla JS file for frontend. No external dependencies (sandbox has no network access).
Used a SQLite CHECK constraint to restrict task statuses to todo, in_progress, and done.
Used JSON request/response bodies and PATCH for partial task edits/status moves.
Validated titles and status values at the API boundary; used parameterized SQLite statements.
Kept the UI as a single static HTML file using vanilla JavaScript and CSS.
Used a status selector on every card to provide direct click-based movement between board columns.
Used an in-process handler harness so API tests exercise the real handler and SQLite logic without opening a network socket.
Verified Python compilation, frontend JavaScript syntax, and whitespace checks in addition to the lifecycle test.

The server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default, which is appropriate for this unauthenticated local Kanban app; it should not be deployed on a public interface without adding authentication and authorization.
Retain the existing 16 KiB request-body limit and resolved-path containment check for static files.
